message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the USA Today High School Player of the Year and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. Over his career, LeBron has played for the Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers. He has won four NBA championships (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020) and earned four NBA Most Valuable Player awards (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013). Known for his versatility, athleticism, court vision, and basketball IQ, he has been selected to numerous All‑NBA teams and has been named an NBA All‑Star 19 times (as of 2024).

Beyond the court, LeBron is also known for his philanthropy, notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise School” in Akron to support at-risk youth. He has also pursued acting, producing, and business ventures, including a partnership with Nike and ownership stakes in media companies. His influence extends into social activism, particularly around issues of racial justice and education.
